    Structural mask on the input grid

    Source: R/coords_mask.R
    mssr_mask.Rd

    Selects exactly ceiling(fraction * n) pixels of a region with the highest MSSR values, on the input grid (amplified results are averaged back over each input pixel's children; this needs grid = "extent"). Pixels tied at the cut are chosen by a seeded random permutation, without changing the caller's random-number state or depending on its RNGkind(). Floating-point noise within eight machine epsilons relative to the quota is snapped to a positive integer before rounding up. Every positive fraction selects at least one pixel. Flat maps can yield masks chosen entirely by ties; such masks are not detected foreground or cell instances.

    Usage

    mssr_mask(result, fraction = 0.5, region = NULL, seed = 1L)

    Arguments

    result

    An mssr_result.

    fraction

    Fraction of the region to keep, in (0, 1].

    region

    Optional logical matrix with the input dimensions; defaults to the whole frame.

    seed

    Whole number used for tie-breaking.

    Value

    A logical matrix (input dimensions) with attributes coverage (selected share of the region), tie_fraction, cut_relative (0 when no score in the region is positive) and n_region.

    Details

    Use the mask to measure the original data, e.g. mean(x[mask]). A mask changes which pixels are measured; it does not make MSSR values quantitative, and selecting pixels by MSSR is not known to improve any downstream analysis. MSSR maps often contain many exact zeros, so check tie_fraction: it is the share of the selected pixels that were decided by random tie-breaking (0 when the cut falls between distinct values; only exact ties count). Also check cut_relative, the lowest selected score divided by the highest score in the region. Interpolation and rounding leave many tiny positive values (often below 1e-6 of the maximum) where MSSR found no structure; they rank above exact zeros without counting as ties, so a small cut_relative means the mask reaches beyond the structure. Both mask and coordinate consumers reject nonfinite values or inconsistent grid metadata. This checks the stored matrix/grid contract, not authenticity of the image, parameters or review status.

    Examples

    x <- matrix(runif(400), 20, 20)
m <- mssr_mask(mssr(x, fwhm = 3), fraction = 0.5)
attr(m, "tie_fraction")
#> [1] 0
mean(x[m])
#> [1] 0.7685152
